monitoring.title: Scorecard monitoring
monitoring.subtitle: How each scorecard version is scoring and performing. Figures are recomputed on every load.
monitoring.explain: As of {asOf}. A loan counts as bad when it reached {dpd}+ days past due within {months} months of disbursement; only loans disbursed at least that long ago (mature) count towards bad rates, Gini, AUC and KS. Stability compares the grade mix of applications scored {baselineFrom} – {baselineTo} (baseline) with {recentFrom} – {recentTo} (recent). Challenger rows are shadow evaluations: they are scored alongside the champion but never affect a decision, so their approval figures reflect the champion’s decisions.

LendingPages.workflows: Origination workflows: optional checks and amount-based approval levels.

LendingPages.auditTrail: Every lending action and policy decision, with the configuration versions in force at the time.

import.title: Import a file
import.subtitle: Lines that name a live loan post repayments; every other line is held in unidentified payments with its reason. A file or line sent twice is only applied once.
import.settlementFormat1: Header row with these columns, in any order: reference, loan_ref, amount, currency, value_date, channel_txn_id, and optionally payer_name. Lines starting with # are ignored.
import.settlementFormat2: loan_ref is the loan account reference (blank if unknown — the line goes to suspense). channel_txn_id identifies the payment at the channel: the same id is never applied twice. Value dates must be within the last 30 days.
import.payrollFormat1: Header row: employee_ref, amount and at least one of national_id / loan_ref per line. The employer, period, currency and value date apply to every line.
import.payrollFormat2: A line by national id is applied when the borrower has exactly one live loan in the file currency. The national id is not stored, only a blind index and its last digits.
import.importedBeforeBody: Nothing was applied again; this is the original import.

subtitle.INVOICE_FINANCE: Advances against approved invoices; the debtor’s payment repays the advance and fee, and the balance goes to the borrower (TV-20).
subtitle.FACTORING: Invoices bought from the seller: the debtor is notified and pays the factor; the fee and advance are repaid first and the balance goes to the seller.
subtitle.SUPPLY_CHAIN: The buyer’s programme: invoices it has approved are paid to its suppliers early at a discount; the buyer pays the face at maturity.
subtitle.FORFAITING: Avalised bills and notes bought without recourse at a discount; the obligor pays the face at maturity.
